findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by processes on the instance and is commonly exposed through instance/cloud-init logs, increasing the risk of credential disclosure.

`publicly_accessible = true` assigns the RDS instance a public network address. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, this removes a network boundary and makes exposure dependent on present and future security-group rules.
`storage_encrypted = false` leaves the RDS database storage and its automated backups unencrypted at rest, exposing stored data if underlying storage or backups are accessed improperly.

The EC2-assumable application role is granted `s3:*`, `ec2:*`, and `rds:*` on every resource. A compromise of the application server would grant broad control over EC2, RDS, and S3 resources, including likely privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration paths.

MySQL port 3306 is open to every address in the VPC CIDR rather than being restricted to the application security group or a narrowly defined set of clients. Any compromised or unauthorized workload in the VPC can attempt to connect to the database.

The MySQL parameter group does not set `require_secure_transport=ON`, while the application connects with `mysqli_connect` without TLS settings. Consequently, database credentials and application data can be transmitted without encryption over the network.
